video_title: Why Image Generation Needs More Than Bigger Models
gist: Qualcomm VP of Technology Fati Periqi walks through four CVPR image-generation papers (DisCo, ArtiCan, PixelRush, InverField) whose common thread is that photorealism is solved but controllability, resolution and on-device efficiency are not, and that all three are fixable by changing objectives, decomposition and initialization around a frozen base model rather than training bigger models. Concrete claims include ~99 unique-face accuracy from GRPO diversity rewards, 4-16 megapixel generation at ~35x speedup (10 minutes to ~20 seconds) via latent-space patching, and 5x faster on-device Wan video generation with no cloud dependency.

insights.claim: Text-to-image models have effectively solved photorealism but remain unsolved on controllability, identity distinctness, resolution above 1K, and on-device efficiency, which is where the remaining research and product value sits.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: Model-quality benchmarks are saturating; differentiation in imaging AI is shifting to control, resolution and runtime cost rather than raw sample realism.
insights.quote: The lighting looks you know natural right the details look right and the overall quality can be amazing

insights.claim: Essentially every leading image model tested, including GPT-based generation, Nano Banana, Flux and HiDream, produces near-identical cookie-cutter faces when asked for multiple people in one image.
insights.speaker: Sam Charrington (host)
insights.so_what: A shared, industry-wide failure mode means the fix is a post-training objective any vendor could adopt, so identity diversity is a temporary and copyable differentiator, not a durable moat.
insights.quote: you look at these images and it's like the same person cookie cutter across the entire group

insights.claim: Cloud-hosted image models are still effectively capped around 1K x 1K resolution, a limitation the speaker says has not previously been addressed by anyone.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: A concrete unmet spec: whoever ships reliable multi-megapixel generation cheaply gets a defensible claim in print, design and pro-imaging markets.
insights.quote: most of the models still are limited to 1K 1K resolution but then you want to go beyond that that is a challenge which has not been actually addressed before

insights.claim: The identity-duplication failure is not an image-quality or architecture problem but a missing training objective, because existing losses reward realism and prompt matching while never explicitly rewarding diversity between generated people.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: Reframes model shortcomings as cheap post-training fixes rather than expensive retraining, compressing the capex needed to close visible capability gaps.
insights.quote: existing training objectives focus heavily on the realism and matching the user prompt, but they don't explicitly encourage diversity

themes.theme: RL post-training beats bigger models and more data

insights.claim: Qualcomm's DisCo work keeps a frozen base text-to-image model and fine-tunes it with GRPO reinforcement learning against explicit rewards for intra-image face diversity, inter-run diversity, correct subject count, and retained image quality.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: The GRPO recipe that reshaped LLM post-training is now migrating to diffusion; expect a wave of cheap RL-tuned image model variants rather than new foundation models.
insights.quote: Instead of you know creating a completely new T2I model, we kept the underlying model and fine-tune it with reinforcement learning.

insights.claim: Adding a desired image attribute as an RL reward requires very little data and makes the fine-tune affordable, which is why Qualcomm rejects the alternative of collecting large new datasets of multi-person images.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: Lowers the cost floor for attribute-specific model customization, favoring firms with tuning pipelines over firms with data-scale advantages.
insights.quote: you can incorporate such objectives in addition to overall let's say perception or image quality uh objective when we are training such models but you do not need a lot of data

insights.claim: The host explicitly framed objective engineering as anti-bitter-lesson and argued for simply collecting more face-heavy data, and the guest pushed back that data scaling is unnecessary when objectives are specified correctly.
insights.speaker: Sam Charrington (host)
insights.so_what: A live disagreement about whether scale or objective design drives the next gains in generative vision; the answer determines whether compute demand or algorithm talent is the binding constraint.
insights.quote: it seems like tuning the objective for all of the possible ways that you might want images to kind of generate correctly seems uh you know not just difficult but like anti-bitter lesson

insights.claim: Curriculum learning, starting with simple scenes and escalating complexity, is what makes reinforcement-learning fine-tuning of image models stable in practice, moving it from a long-theoretical idea to a shipped training technique.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: Training-stability tricks are becoming the differentiator in RL-for-diffusion; watch curriculum adoption as a signal that RL post-training is industrializing.
insights.quote: starting from simpler scenes and gradually increasing complexity makes learning this reinforcement learning much more stable

insights.claim: Qualcomm released a new benchmark called DiverseHumans specifically to standardize measurement of identity diversity in generated images, alongside the DisCo paper.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: Vendors that define the benchmark tend to define the leaderboard; a new axis of measurement can reset competitive rankings in image generation.
insights.quote: We call it as diverse humans.

insights.claim: DisCo reaches roughly 99 on unique face accuracy while the base models it started from score 10 to 20 percentage points lower, and it also improves human preference score rather than trading quality for diversity.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: Quantifies that a control objective can be added without the usual quality tax, weakening the argument that controllability must cost fidelity.
insights.quote: Disco is around 99 but you know kind of like the models that these models where we started that doesn't have such explicit diversity objective they are very low

insights.claim: The diversity reward is built entirely from off-the-shelf components: a face detector to get bounding boxes, an ArcFace-style embedding into a canonical space, and pairwise similarity scoring across detected faces.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: Reward functions for visual attributes can be assembled from commodity CV models, so the barrier to replicating this class of result is low.
insights.quote: there is a face detector applied and this is off the shop

insights.claim: The generalizable lesson the guest draws is that many apparent model failures are missed training objectives rather than architectural limits, so the fix is how the objective and data are presented to the algorithm.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: A diagnostic heuristic for evaluating AI companies: capability gaps fixable by objective design imply fast catch-up, not durable leads.
insights.quote: it is not mainly an architecture limit itation but it is how you are providing this objective and training data to the algorithm

themes.theme: Split planning from rendering, then route across specialists

insights.claim: Asking one image model to simultaneously parse the prompt, decide subject count, plan composition, reason about interactions, preserve specific identities and render pixels is too much for a single model, and decomposition is the way forward.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: The monolithic-model era in imaging is being questioned by a major silicon vendor, pointing to pipeline architectures where value accrues to orchestration rather than weights.
insights.quote: Maybe we are also asking a single model to solve too many difficult problems at once

insights.claim: Qualcomm's ArtiCan splits generation into an architect that produces scene structure and face placement coordinates and an artist that renders photorealistic pixels conditioned on those locations, mirroring how a human artist plans before painting.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: A concrete blueprint for two-stage generative pipelines that could become the standard architecture for controllable image and video products.
insights.quote: we separate uh planning from rendering similar to how a human artist would work

insights.claim: The architect stage does no learning at inference time and simply emits coordinate tuples such as three XY centroids for a three-person prompt, with GRPO applied only during offline fine-tuning of the artist.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: Inference cost stays close to a single-model pass, so the controllability gains are essentially free at serving time, which matters for on-device deployment economics.
insights.quote: So this GRPO is on the finetuning offline field

insights.claim: ArtiCan's reward function stacks composition correctness, identity matching against provided reference faces, head pose, subject count accuracy, prompt alignment and human perception score into one GRPO objective.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: Shows multi-objective reward stacking working in production research, the same pattern that will govern controllable video generation next.

insights.claim: ArtiCan's training identities are synthetic faces generated by another model rather than real people, which makes the training pipeline fully automatable and sidesteps consented-face-data collection.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: Removes a legal and data-acquisition bottleneck around face datasets, reducing a key regulatory risk for identity-conditioned generation products.
insights.quote: these are not necessarily real faces I mean to automate the training process

insights.claim: Qualcomm is actively building an agentic orchestration pipeline that routes an incoming prompt to specialized image models such as a diversity-tuned model or a text-rendering model and then orchestrates the final generation.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: Signals that even chipmakers expect inference to become multi-model orchestration, increasing per-image compute and favoring flexible NPU workloads over one big model.
insights.quote: we are working on such aantic also pipelines depending on the input it goes or determines the right tool

insights.claim: The guest believes specialization plus routing, not a single universal model, will be the ultimate solution for top-tier image generation because one size does not fit everyone.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: Contradicts the one-frontier-model narrative and supports investment in model-portfolio and routing infrastructure rather than winner-take-all model bets.
insights.quote: I think this is going to be the ultimate solution you know one uh maybe size doesn't fit everyone if you really really want to generate something amazing top of the line

themes.theme: Breaking the 1K ceiling with latent-space patching

insights.claim: PixelRush generates 4 to 16 megapixel images by rendering a 1K base image with any existing model, upsampling in RGB with an off-the-shelf super-resolution step, then patchifying into latent space for guided refinement before VAE decoding.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: A model-agnostic wrapper that multiplies output resolution without retraining is immediately deployable across the entire installed base of image models.
insights.quote: you can still use any of those models that you have and then uh follow our pipeline we discussed in the paper so you can use that model still generate let's say four times 16 times more pixels

insights.claim: PixelRush holds the latent space at the original 1K dimensionality instead of scaling it with output resolution as baselines do, which is the specific mechanism that avoids the memory blowup blocking high-resolution generation on handsets.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: Memory, not FLOPs, is the binding constraint for on-device generative imaging, which shapes which mobile SoC specs actually matter.
insights.quote: the baseline actually does that you know kind of like they just uh make the latence space larger proportional to the target uh output resolution which is not we wanted to do

insights.claim: PixelRush claims roughly 35x speedup on high-resolution generation, taking a task from about 10 minutes down to around 20 seconds.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: Crossing from minutes to sub-30-seconds is the threshold that turns high-res generation from a batch job into an interactive on-device feature.
insights.quote: It's maybe 35 times faster. You know, from let's say uh 10 minutes to uh around 20 seconds type of you know acceleration

insights.claim: Patch seams are resolved by injecting more noise near patch boundaries and less at patch centers while blending in latent space, because blending in pixel space would visibly blur the seams instead.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: The non-obvious engineering trick that makes tiled high-res generation viable, and a template competitors will copy for tiled video generation.
insights.quote: allow algorithm to generate uh more noise towards the boundary but in the center of the pages you know kind of like um be maybe less at a less lesser degree

insights.claim: Upsampled patches are deliberately re-noised with guided semantic noise so the diffusion model can invent genuinely new high-resolution texture rather than merely sharpening an interpolated image.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: Distinguishes true detail synthesis from upscaling, the quality claim that will decide whether on-device high-res output competes with cloud rendering.
insights.quote: these images are not really super resolved in the way that we wanted because they are just upsamples

insights.claim: InverField addresses image-to-image inpainting rather than text-to-image, targeting object removal and insertion where current tools leave visible texture mismatch and boundary artifacts that make the feature a toy rather than a usable product.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: Editing, not generation, is the consumer-photography use case with the largest gap between demo and daily utility, and therefore the largest near-term product upside.
insights.quote: it is like a toy you know yeah you can do that but I'm not going to really use it

insights.claim: InverField inverts the real input image into image-specific noise in about 60 milliseconds and initializes the diffusion process from that inverted noise plus fresh random noise inside the mask, changing only initialization rather than the underlying model.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: A near-free inference-time change that upgrades any existing editing model, so incumbents can adopt it without retraining and the advantage decays fast.
insights.quote: I don't need to change the original model. I can still you know I change the way that I initialize the diffusion in this uh painting

insights.claim: Because the background is represented by inverted image-specific noise rather than random noise, InverField preserves the background while still letting it influence the masked region, eliminating boundary artifacts and producing seamless harmonization.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: Boundary artifacts are the single most common tell of AI editing; removing them structurally raises the bar for provenance and detection tooling.
insights.quote: there's no boundary artifacts anymore because we have two noise

themes.theme: On-device generation as Qualcomm's strategic wedge

insights.claim: Qualcomm presented more than 20 papers at this year's CVPR, with the imaging work uniformly aimed at removing the need for a cloud service provider.
insights.speaker: Sam Charrington (host)
insights.so_what: Sustained research volume aimed at edge inference is the tell for Qualcomm's positioning against cloud-hosted generative services.
insights.quote: whose team presented more than 20 papers at this year's CVPR

insights.claim: Qualcomm claims it can run the open-source Wan video generation model roughly five times faster and squeeze it into a memory-limited device, removing the cloud requirement for video generation on PCs, laptops and phones.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: Open-weight video models plus edge acceleration is the combination that would move video-generation inference demand off cloud GPUs and onto client silicon.
insights.quote: you can like five times faster and then put it into squeeze it into your memory limited device. You don't need to run uh it on the cloud

insights.claim: Qualcomm's other two video papers attack attention cost directly through a recurrent hybrid attention scheme and an attention surgery technique, on the premise that attention dominates compute in video generation.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: Attention-cost reduction is where the on-device video generation battle is being fought, a leading indicator for which workloads mobile NPUs are being designed around.
insights.quote: attention surgery because attention takes a lot of compute

insights.claim: Across all four imaging papers the deliberate pattern is to leave the base generative model untouched and add value through objectives, decomposition, or initialization, implying Qualcomm sees foundation image models as commoditized substrate.
insights.speaker: Fati Periqi (Qualcomm VP of Technology)
insights.so_what: If the model layer is substrate and the pipeline layer is the product, competitive advantage in imaging accrues to whoever controls the device and the orchestration stack.
insights.quote: we didn't want people to uh go and have to find fine-tune those models
